sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: remaining equipment, defensive driving, distractions, steering and scanning
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from this section's selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge or memory.
The first selected page opens with the tail of a safety belt sentence carried over from the previous page; that fragment is not taught here [A01].
Two parentheses on the first selected page (the windshield line and the hazard warning line) open without closing in the extracted text; the rules were read from the surrounding words only [A01].
The manual says window tint is legal only within certain limits but does not print those limits, so no tint measurement is taught (verify AZ-EQDD-D-TINT) [A01].
One sentence about minor distractions on the last selected page is garbled in the extracted text and is not restated; the distraction list itself is clear [A03].
Originality: every statement is reworded from the cited page; no manual sentence, table, image or official test question is reproduced.
Exam numbers: the manual prints no question count, passing score, item format or time limit, so none is stated anywhere in this section; the typed debts live in part A.
External review: restating published Arizona traffic and licensing rules needs no clinical or legal sign-off; none is requested.

corpus_stability.reason: The Arizona Driver License Manual carries one revision line on its contents page (Revised September 2026) and points to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for current law; nothing in the selected pages signals more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: The manual states that sun-screening tint on windows and windshields is legal only within certain limits and defers to Arizona law; confirm the current limits from Arizona Revised Statutes or an official ADOT page before teaching any value.
